members.title: Run quarterly line-manager reviews with a timed central workflow
members.statement: The performance team runs reviews every quarter, line managers own rating-producing scorecards, and employees receive grades and feedback after central calculation, calibration and top-management approval.
members.relevance: Preserves cadence, responsibilities, timing, feedback routes and the exception for optional colleague input.

facets.text: Review every quarter so recognition of strong work and reactions to underperformance are both quick.
Stage 1 lasts 1–2 weeks: the performance team requests reviews from line managers, who gather feedback and complete scorecards based on observable behaviour.

Managers may ask colleagues, other managers or functional leads for additional reviews, but these do not themselves influence the rating; the line manager completes the scorecard that produces the final grade.
This is not a 360 review. The manual says employee-to-employee reviews tend to be overly generous, provide limited useful feedback and consume employee time.
The chart allocates one week to central grade calculation/calibration, followed by top-management approval and one week for managers to deliver grades and one-to-one debriefing.
Stage 3 lasts one week: send the final results by email and let employees discuss them with their manager in the weekly one-to-one.
The results materially affect career trajectory and compensation and can lead to promotion or a PIP; the process is therefore tied to subsequent action.
The overview calls for a simple, quick, standardised quarterly review process that saves managers' time.
